findings.title: Negative queryset slicing will raise AssertionError at runtime
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is True and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code passes a negative `start_offset` to `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django's QuerySet does not support negative indexing — it raises `AssertionError("Negative indexing is not supported.")` in `Query.set_limits()`. The comment claiming 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is incorrect. This will produce a 500 error for any request that triggers this path (which is exposed via the audit logs endpoint when `optimized_pagination=true` is passed by a superuser or org admin).

findings.title: Eviction via zpopmin can remove the root span, causing data loss in flushed segments
findings.body: The eviction logic uses `zpopmin` which removes elements with the lowest scores (i.e., earliest `end_timestamp_precise`). If the root span (segment span) has one of the earliest end timestamps in a segment exceeding 1000 spans, it will be evicted. The `has_root_span` flag is stored in a separate key and survives eviction, so the segment will still be flushed with the shorter root timeout, but the root span's payload will be missing from the output. Downstream consumers will receive a segment without its root span, which violates the segment contract and can cause data integrity issues in traces.

findings.title: BasePaginator.get_result allows negative offset when is_prev is True
findings.body: The change `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` means that when `cursor.is_prev` is True, the raw `cursor.offset` is used without clamping. Since cursor values are parsed from user-supplied strings via `Cursor.from_string` (which does `int(bits[1])`), a malicious or malformed cursor like `0:-5:1` will produce a negative offset. Django will then raise `AssertionError` on the queryset slice, resulting in an unhandled 500 error instead of a proper 400 validation response.

findings.title: Optimized paginator with broken negative offset feature is gated only by org admin access
findings.body: The `enable_advanced` check allows any organization member with `has_global_access` (org admins) to trigger the `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `enable_advanced_features=True`. Since the negative offset handling in that paginator is broken (causes AssertionError), any org admin can trigger a 500 error by crafting a cursor with a negative offset value. This could be used as a denial-of-service vector against the audit logs endpoint.

findings.title: Redirect depth limit silently reduced from 10000 to 1000, removing explanatory comment
findings.body: The redirect resolution loop limit was reduced from 10000 to 1000, and the comment explaining the tradeoff ('theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly') was removed. For traces with redirect chains deeper than 1000 (which can happen with long-running traces that undergo many rebalancing/merging operations), spans will fail to be joined into the correct segment. The original comment acknowledged this as a known limitation at 10k; reducing to 1k increases the probability of incorrect segment assembly without any documented justification.

findings.title: max_segment_spans parameter is now unused but still accepted in constructor
findings.body: The `max_segment_spans` parameter (default 1001) is still accepted in `SpansBuffer.__init__` and stored as `self.max_segment_spans`, but the check that used it (`if len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans`) was removed from `_load_segment_data` since eviction is now handled in the Lua script. This dead parameter is confusing for callers and the `__reduce__` method doesn't include it, meaning unpickled instances will always get the default value regardless of what was originally configured.

findings.title: __reduce__ passes redis_ttl as segment_page_size due to positional argument mismatch
findings.body: The `__reduce__` method returns `(SpansBuffer, (self.assigned_shards, self.span_buffer_timeout_secs, self.span_buffer_root_timeout_secs, self.redis_ttl))`. However, the constructor's 4th positional parameter is `segment_page_size`, not `redis_ttl`. This means when a `SpansBuffer` is unpickled (e.g., in multiprocessing), `segment_page_size` will be set to the value of `redis_ttl` (3600 instead of 100), and `redis_ttl` will get its default value. This is a pre-existing bug but is relevant since this PR modifies the class.
